h1: Internal air volume versus an expansion vessel
title: Air Gap vs Expansion Vessel | Cylinder Guide
description: Understand internal air volume versus an expansion vessel with clear model-aware information and practical questions for your cylinder engineer.
answer: Both arrangements accommodate expansion where designed, but they are not interchangeable maintenance procedures and must be matched to the installed model.

sections.heading: The key distinction
paragraphs: Some domestic Megaflo products use internal expansion provision. Other cylinders and certain named Megaflo ranges use an external vessel. A hidden vessel can also be part of another manufacturer design, so appearance is an unreliable guide.

sections.heading: Apply the information to the installed system
paragraphs: Do not copy an air-gap routine into a vessel recharge or use a universal pressure setting. If a symptom returns, the complete pressure and safety arrangement needs assessment rather than repeated speculative adjustments.

sections.heading: A practical next question
paragraphs: Gather the full model, heating method, recent symptoms and available paperwork. Discuss the scope with a person competent for the actual work. Technical information here supports that conversation and is not a substitute for manufacturer instructions or individual system assessment.

faqs.question: Does every Megaflo product use internal expansion instead of an external vessel?
faqs.answer: No. Expansion arrangements vary by model and range; identify the installed appliance and its matching instructions before planning maintenance.
